JSON missing the schema ({"session_id":"f2-schema","role":5}): the same suppression, naming the field — the file-side ZodError, the other half of the separation. No record: no line at all. proof.criterion: A queued role retry must not stop the heartbeat's interests reconciliation, including the adoptHandoff path.
proof.surface: The same rig: the proxy answering every POST /v1/roles/set with 503 so the retry fails on every tick, and refusing the first GET /v1/interests/<session> so the startup read fails, with the session's interests in the registry changed under it while it runs.
proof.command: the same probe, cases R1 and R3: a topic added to the registry that the session does not follow, then the registry read back from the listener over the next heartbeats
proof.observed: With the claim failing every tick, the registry went from notifications.agent.r3-head, notifications.probe.drifted, notifications.probe.kept to notifications.agent.r3-head, notifications.probe.kept — the reconciliation removed the drifted topic and kept the followed one — and no 'registry heartbeat failed' line was written at all. So the tick ran past transferRole to syncRegisteredInterests on every beat while the role kept failing.
proof.negativeControl: The previous head's bundle in the same shape: the drifted topic was still in the registry after two more heartbeats, and 'envoy-channel: registry heartbeat failed (POST …/v1/roles/set failed with 503 …); retrying every heartbeat' was written once — the tick ending at transferRole, which is the starvation this change removes. One honest limit of the rig: a message published to a topic the registry lists reached the session on both heads, so delivery does not discriminate here — the listener fans out server-side. The registry drift is what does.

correctionInThisRound.what: I first recorded a failure that did not exist: that this round's code had no CI because the branch head carries skip-checks: true.
correctionInThisRound.why_it_was_wrong: I ran `gh run list --commit 301288e631cb` with the abbreviated sha. That field matches the full forty-character sha only, so gh answered with nothing and I read 'no runs' where the right reading was 'no answer to that query'. With the full sha, 301288e631cbbbd02f3fb22673bf42d00c658d55, every run is there, and `gh run view` on each gives headSha=301288e631cb. My second reading, `gh pr checks 2154` showing one check, was consistent with the error because it reads the pull request's head, which is the handoff commit a handoff-only push correctly leaves without runs.
correctionInThisRound.what_was_actually_right: The implementer pushed the code commit with no trailer, which started CI at its own sha, and pushed the handoff commit afterwards as a handoff-only push with the trailer. That is the rule as written, and the daemon carries the code head's verdict to the handoff head.
correctionInThisRound.kept_here_on_purpose: So the next reader can tell a real CI gap from this one: the test is the full sha, and `gh run list` with an abbreviated one proves nothing either way.

classNote: The round-four authorship defect stands on its own: a code commit kept the review App as author because handoff_complete guards the handoff commit of a push and nothing guards the code commit beside it. I had paired it with the trailer reading above as a second instance of one class; with the trailer reading withdrawn, the class has one member, and the retro learning should say so rather than count my misreading as evidence.
